library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chu_2026_amphotericinB_liposomal"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chu_2026_amphotericinB_liposomal"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70124> (open access)

Chu et al. fitted a single joint PK-PD model to plasma total amphotericin B,
plasma miltefosine and a skin parasite score in patients with post-kala-azar
dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL). Its central feature is a feedback loop: liposomal
amphotericin B (LAmB) is taken up by the mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS)
with a capacity `Bmax(t)` that grows with the parasite burden, the drug in the
MPS clears the parasites, and as the parasites clear the capacity shrinks so
that more drug stays in plasma. The model is packaged as one file because the
three parts were estimated jointly and are coupled through `Bmax(t)` and the
parasite kill terms.

# Population

Sixty patients with PKDL from a phase II randomized trial in India (n = 50;
two sites) and Bangladesh (n = 10), allocated 30/30 to LAmB monotherapy
(AmBisome 4 mg/kg on days 1, 4, 8, 11 and 15; total 20 mg/kg) or the same
LAmB regimen plus oral miltefosine twice daily for 21 days (Chu 2026 Methods
and Table 1). Median age 22.5 years (IQR 15.8-36.3; 30% aged 18 or younger),
53.3% female, median body weight 45.5 kg (IQR 40.3-55), fat-free mass 39.2 kg
(IQR 34.1-45) and BMI 19.0 kg/m^2. Baseline skin qPCR was a median 1050
parasites/ug DNA (IQR 156-5920) and the baseline PKDL lesion score a median
175 squares on the body map (IQR 75.5-262). The analysis used 646 amphotericin
B and 143 miltefosine plasma samples and 177 parasite scores (baseline, day 30
and 3 months).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Chu_2026_amphotericinB_liposomal")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(mps)` | saturable uptake `kin * A_central * (1 - A_MPS / Bmax(t))`, release `kout * A_MPS`, linear `CL` | Eq. 1; Figure 2 |
| `bmax_t` | `Bmax,base * (WT/45) + Bmax,disease * A_parasite(t)` | Eq. 3; Table 2 footnote a |
| `d/dt(log10_parasites)` | `-(lambda_LAmB * A_MPS + lambda_MF * C_MF) * A_parasite` | Eq. 4 |
| `f(depot_miltefosine)` | `TVF * CumDose^COV` | Supplementary Methods S3, Equation S1 (day > 7 form) |
| `lcl` | log(0.3) L/h at 45 kg | Table 2 |
| `lvc` | log(3.1) L at 45 kg | Table 2 |
| `lkin_mps` | log(0.53) 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lkout_mps` | log(0.018) 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lbmax_mps` | log(10) mg at 45 kg, fixed | Table 2; Results |
| `lbmax_mps_disease` | log(16) mg per log10 unit | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_bmax_mps` | 0.75, 1, 1 (fixed) | Table 2 footnote a; Results |
| `lcl_miltefosine` | log(0.086) L/h at FFM 40 kg | Table 2; Supplementary Results S1 |
| `lvc_miltefosine` | log(20) L at FFM 40 kg | Table 2 |
| `lq_miltefosine` | log(0.0012) L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvp_miltefosine` | log(1.9) L at FFM 40 kg | Table 2 |
| `lka_miltefosine` | log(0.225) 1/h, fixed | Table 2 footnote d; Supplementary Methods S3 |
| `lfdepot_miltefosine` | log(1), fixed | Supplementary Methods S3 |
| `e_dose_mf_cum_mgkg_fdepot` | -0.13, fixed | Table 2 footnote d; Supplementary Results S1 |
| `e_ffm_cl_miltefosine`, `e_ffm_vc_vp_miltefosine` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Table 2 footnote c; Supplementary Methods S3 |
| `lslope_amphotericinb` | log(1.6e-4) 1/(mg h) | Table 2 |
| `lslope_miltefosine` | log(4.9e-5) L/(mg h) | Table 2 |
| `lrbase` | log(4.7) log10 units | Table 2 |
| `etalcl + etalvc` | 43% and 32% CV, correlation 0.92 | Table 2 and footnote b |
| `etalkin_mps` | 59% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalbmax_mps_disease` | 40% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalcl_miltefosine` | 19% CV | Table 2; Supplementary Results S1 |
| `etalslope_amphotericinb` | 49% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalrbase` | 350% CV | Table 2 |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.22; 0.25 mg/L fixed | Table 2; Methods (LLOQ/2) |
| `propSd_miltefosine` | 0.27 | Table 2 |
| `addSd_log10_parasites` | 1.1 log10 units | Table 2 |

Every CV% is converted with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, following the
exponential BSV model stated in the Methods.

# Event-table helper

All simulations share one builder. LAmB is a 2-hour IV infusion into
`central`; miltefosine is given twice daily into `depot_miltefosine`.
Observation rows sit on the `central` ODE state and carry `dvid = 1`, because
the model declares three endpoints (`Cc`, `Cc_miltefosine`,
`log10_parasites`); every observation row returns all three, plus `mps` and
`bmax_t`.

```{r helper}
mod <- readModelDb("Chu_2026_amphotericinB_liposomal")

# `lamb_days` are 1-based treatment days; `mf_mg_day` = 0 gives monotherapy.
make_events <- function(id, wt, ffm, lamb_mgkg, lamb_days, mf_mg_day,
                        obs_times, mf_days = 21) {
  lamb <- tibble(
    id = id, time = 24 * (lamb_days - 1), amt = lamb_mgkg * wt,
    rate = lamb_mgkg * wt / 2, cmt = "central", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  mf <- if (mf_mg_day > 0) {
    tibble(
      id = id, time = sort(c(24 * (seq_len(mf_days) - 1), 24 * (seq_len(mf_days) - 1) + 12)),
      amt = mf_mg_day / 2, rate = 0, cmt = "depot_miltefosine", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  }
  obs <- tibble(
    id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central",
    evid = 0L, dvid = 1L
  )
  bind_rows(lamb, mf, obs) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(
      WT = wt, FFM = ffm,
      # Running total of weight-normalized daily miltefosine doses including
      # the current day (Equation S1). It must stay positive, so monotherapy
      # rows carry a placeholder of 1; f(depot_miltefosine) is only ever
      # evaluated on miltefosine dose records.
      DOSE_MF_CUM_MGKG = if (mf_mg_day > 0) {
        pmin(floor(time / 24) + 1, mf_days) * mf_mg_day / wt
      } else {
        1
      }
    )
}
```

# Typical patient: the PK-parasite feedback (Figure 3)

Figure 3 simulates a typical patient (45 kg, fat-free mass 40 kg, baseline
log10 parasite score 4.7) on the trial regimen, alone or with miltefosine
150 mg/day.

```{r typical}
typ_mod <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 30 * 24, by = 0.25), seq(31 * 24, 90 * 24, by = 24))))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  make_events(1L, 45, 40, 4, c(1, 4, 8, 11, 15), 0, obs_grid) |> mutate(arm = "LAmB monotherapy"),
  make_events(2L, 45, 40, 4, c(1, 4, 8, 11, 15), 150, obs_grid) |> mutate(arm = "LAmB + miltefosine")
)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ_mod, ev_typ, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
```

The daily AUC of plasma amphotericin B (the bars in Figure 3) comes from
PKNCA over consecutive 24-hour intervals:

```{r typical-daily-auc}
conc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 30 * 24) |>
  select(id, arm, time, Cc)
dose_typ <- ev_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "central") |>
  select(id, arm, time, amt)
iv_daily <- data.frame(
  start = 24 * (0:29), end = 24 * (1:30), auclast = TRUE
)
nca_daily <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_typ, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_typ, amt ~ time | arm + id),
  intervals = iv_daily
))
daily_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_daily) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  transmute(arm, day = start / 24 + 1, auc_mgday = PPORRES / 24)
```

```{r fig3, fig.height = 5}
typ_long <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time <= 90 * 24) |>
  transmute(
    arm, day = time / 24,
    `Bmax in MPS (mg)` = bmax_t,
    `AmB in MPS (mg)` = mps,
    `Parasite score (log10) x 10` = 10 * log10_parasites
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(arm, day), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "value")
ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = daily_auc, aes(x = day - 0.5, y = auc_mgday),
    fill = "#E6A65D", width = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_line(data = typ_long, aes(day, value, colour = quantity), linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Amount (mg), AUC (mg/L*day) or 10 x log10 score",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Chu 2026. Bars: daily plasma AUC (mg/L*day)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The paper states three numbers for this simulation. Under combination
therapy `Bmax(t)` on day 15 is down to 22% of its starting value (Results:
"a 22% decrease in Bmax by day 15"; Figure 3 shows the curve falling from
about 88 mg to about 20 mg, so the figure is the remaining fraction, not the
drop), and the day-15 plasma AUC0-24 is 54% higher than on day 1.
The plateaus after treatment are read from Figure 3.

```{r fig3-check}
bmax0 <- sim_typ |> filter(time == 0) |> select(arm, bmax0 = bmax_t)
bmax_d15 <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time == 14 * 24) |>
  left_join(bmax0, by = "arm") |>
  transmute(arm, bmax_d15 = bmax_t, frac_remaining = bmax_t / bmax0)
auc_ratio <- daily_auc |>
  filter(day %in% c(1, 15)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = day, values_from = auc_mgday, names_prefix = "day") |>
  mutate(ratio = day15 / day1)
plateau <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time == 90 * 24) |>
  select(arm, bmax_day90 = bmax_t, log10_parasites_day90 = log10_parasites)
fig3_tbl <- bmax_d15 |>
  left_join(auc_ratio, by = "arm") |>
  left_join(plateau, by = "arm")
fig3_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Bmax day 15 (mg)" = bmax_d15,
    "Bmax day 15 / day 1" = frac_remaining,
    "AUC0-24 day 1 (mg/L*day)" = day1, "AUC0-24 day 15 (mg/L*day)" = day15,
    "AUC ratio day 15 / day 1" = ratio, "Bmax day 90 (mg)" = bmax_day90,
    "log10 score day 90" = log10_parasites_day90
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

combo <- fig3_tbl |> filter(arm == "LAmB + miltefosine")
mono <- fig3_tbl |> filter(arm == "LAmB monotherapy")
stopifnot(
  # Results: Bmax down to 22% of baseline by day 15 (combination).
  abs(combo$frac_remaining - 0.22) < 0.03,
  # Results: 54% higher systemic AUC0-24 on day 15 than on day 1.
  abs(combo$ratio / 1.54 - 1) < 0.10,
  # Figure 3 plateaus: Bmax about 15 mg (monotherapy) and 11 mg (combination).
  abs(mono$bmax_day90 - 15) < 2,
  abs(combo$bmax_day90 - 11) < 2
)
```

# Alternative LAmB regimens (Figure 4)

Figure 4 compares four LAmB monotherapy regimens in the typical patient:
the trial regimen, half the per-dose amount on the same schedule, a shortened
schedule and a 10 mg/kg single dose. The comparison values were read from the
figure at day 45 by the maintainers.

```{r fig4-sim}
regimens <- tibble(
  regimen = c(
    "4 mg/kg x 5 over 15 days", "2 mg/kg x 5 over 15 days",
    "5 mg/kg x 4 over 7 days", "10 mg/kg single dose"
  ),
  mgkg = c(4, 2, 5, 10),
  days = list(c(1, 4, 8, 11, 15), c(1, 4, 8, 11, 15), c(1, 3, 5, 7), 1)
)
grid45 <- seq(0, 45 * 24, by = 0.25)
ev_reg <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_events(i, 45, 40, regimens$mgkg[i], regimens$days[[i]], 0, grid45) |>
    mutate(regimen = regimens$regimen[i])
}))
sim_reg <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ_mod, ev_reg, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen))
```

Cumulative AUCs to day 45, plasma (`Cc`) and MPS amount (`mps`), by PKNCA:

```{r fig4-nca}
dose_reg <- ev_reg |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, regimen, time, amt)
iv45 <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 45 * 24, auclast = TRUE)
nca45 <- function(col) {
  conc <- sim_reg |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) |>
    transmute(id, regimen = as.character(regimen), time, conc = .data[[col]])
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | regimen + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_reg, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
    intervals = iv45
  ))
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
    mutate(PPORRES = PPORRES / 24)
}
sim45 <- bind_rows(
  nca45("Cc") |> mutate(quantity = "Plasma (mg/L*day)"),
  nca45("mps") |> mutate(quantity = "MPS (mg*day)")
) |>
  select(quantity, regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
ref45 <- tibble(
  quantity = rep(c("Plasma (mg/L*day)", "MPS (mg*day)"), each = 4),
  regimen = rep(regimens$regimen, 2),
  auclast = c(124, 62, 125, 62, 670, 655, 580, 515)
)
cmp45 <- ncaComparisonTable(sim45, ref45, by = c("quantity", "regimen"))
knitr::kable(cmp45, caption = "Cumulative AUC 0-45 days: simulated vs digitized Figure 4a-b.")
stopifnot(all(abs(cmp45[["% diff"]] |> sub(pattern = "[*%]", replacement = "") |> as.numeric()) < 10))
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
sim_reg |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, log10_parasites, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Parasite score (log10)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4c of Chu 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

lp45 <- sim_reg |>
  filter(time == 45 * 24) |>
  select(regimen, sim = log10_parasites) |>
  mutate(digitized = c(0.35, 0.37, 0.48, 0.62))
knitr::kable(lp45, digits = 2, caption = "log10 parasite score on day 45 (digitized Figure 4c).")
stopifnot(all(abs(lp45$sim - lp45$digitized) < 0.1))
```

The model reproduces the paper's conclusion: halving the per-dose amount on
the same five-dose schedule halves plasma exposure but leaves MPS exposure and
parasite clearance close to the trial regimen, and it outperforms the same
10 mg/kg total given as a single dose.

# Virtual trial cohort

A stochastic cohort of 100 subjects per arm, with body weight drawn from a
log-normal distribution matched to the Table 1 median and IQR. The paper's
individual heights and sex are not available, so fat-free mass is set to
`WT * 39.2 / 45.5` (the ratio of the Table 1 medians). Weights are kept above
30 kg so the miltefosine dose follows the fixed 100 / 150 mg/day bands; the
allometric miltefosine dosing of patients of 30 kg or less is not
reproduced.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261111)
set.seed(20261111)
n_arm <- 100
wts <- pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(2 * n_arm, log(45.5), 0.23)), 30.5), 80)
obs_vpc <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 24, by = 0.5), seq(14 * 24, 15 * 24, by = 0.5),
  24 * c(2:13, 16:30, 45, 60, 90)
)))
ev_vpc <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(2 * n_arm), function(i) {
  combo <- i > n_arm
  wt <- wts[i]
  mf <- if (!combo) 0 else if (wt >= 45) 150 else 100
  make_events(i, wt, wt * 39.2 / 45.5, 4, c(1, 4, 8, 11, 15), mf, obs_vpc) |>
    mutate(arm = if (combo) "LAmB + miltefosine" else "LAmB monotherapy")
}))
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_vpc, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
```

## Plasma amphotericin B after the first and last dose

```{r vpc-pk}
pk_win <- sim_vpc |>
  filter(time <= 24 | (time >= 14 * 24 & time <= 15 * 24)) |>
  mutate(
    event = if_else(time <= 24, "First dose (day 1)", "Last dose (day 15)"),
    tad = if_else(time <= 24, time, time - 14 * 24)
  ) |>
  group_by(event, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(pk_win, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~event) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma amphotericin B (mg/L)",
    caption = "Median and 90% interval; compare with the observed data in Figure 1a of Chu 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

PKNCA on the first and last dosing interval:

```{r vpc-nca}
conc_vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 15 * 24) |>
  select(id, arm, time, Cc)
dose_vpc <- ev_vpc |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "central") |>
  select(id, arm, time, amt)
iv_vpc <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 14 * 24), end = c(24, 15 * 24),
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_vpc <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_vpc, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_vpc, amt ~ time | arm + id),
  intervals = iv_vpc
))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_vpc) |>
  mutate(day = if_else(start == 0, "day 1", "day 15")) |>
  group_by(arm, day, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Dose" = day, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters per dosing event.")

auc_ratio_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_vpc) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, arm, start, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = start, values_from = PPORRES, names_prefix = "s") |>
  mutate(ratio = s336 / s0)
summary(auc_ratio_ind$ratio)
stopifnot(
  # Abstract: 'a median 54% increase in the systemic LAmB exposure (AUC0-24h)
  # by the end of treatment' (1.46 in the run documented here). The band is
  # wide because the median of 200 ratios with this spread moves by about
  # 0.08 between cohorts; losing the Bmax feedback would put it near 1.
  median(auc_ratio_ind$ratio) > 1.2,
  median(auc_ratio_ind$ratio) < 1.9
)
```

## Plasma miltefosine and parasite score

```{r vpc-pd, fig.height = 4}
mf_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  filter(arm == "LAmB + miltefosine", time %in% (24 * c(7, 14, 21, 28, 45, 60, 90))) |>
  group_by(day = time / 24) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc_miltefosine, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc_miltefosine),
    p95 = quantile(Cc_miltefosine, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(mf_sum, digits = 1, caption = "Simulated plasma miltefosine (mg/L); compare Figure 1b of Chu 2026.")

ps_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  filter(time %in% (24 * c(0, 30, 90))) |>
  group_by(arm, day = time / 24) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(log10_parasites, 0.05), p50 = median(log10_parasites),
    p95 = quantile(log10_parasites, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(ps_sum, digits = 2, caption = "Simulated individual log10 parasite score (no residual error).")
```

The simulated miltefosine levels (5th-95th percentiles about 20-40 mg/L across days 7-21, falling
after the last dose on day 21) match the range of Figure 1b. The parasite
score shows how large the printed between-subject variability of the
baseline is (see the next section): its 90% interval at baseline spans
roughly 0.3-0.6 to 50-80 log10 units. The observed baselines in Figure 1c
lie between about 1.5 and 8 log10 units, and the observed day-30 and
3-month scores (about 1 to 4.5 log10 units) sit well above the typical
prediction of 0.1-0.4. The model reaches them only through that large
baseline variability and the 1.1 log10 additive residual error.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Parasite score on the log10 scale.** Eq. 4 is printed as a first-order
  decline of `A_parasite`. Eq. 3 multiplies the same `A_parasite` by
  `Bmax,disease`, whose units are mg per log10(parasite score) (Table 2).
  The baseline is estimated as 4.7 log10 units, and the residual error is
  additive on the log10 scale. The state is therefore the log10 score itself,
  decaying exponentially toward 0. This reading reproduces the paper's own
  simulations: Figure 3 plateaus and the 22% `Bmax` figure (above), and all
  twelve digitized day-45 values of Figure 4. Integrating Eq. 4 on the linear
  score instead leaves the typical patient near 2 log10 units at 3 months and
  `Bmax` at about 71% of its baseline on day 15, which contradicts Figure 3.
* **"22% decrease in Bmax by day 15".** Figure 3 shows `Bmax(t)` falling to
  about a quarter of its starting value by day 15, so the 22% is the fraction
  remaining, not the size of the drop. The model gives 22% remaining under
  combination therapy and 25% under monotherapy.
* **Baseline BSV of 350% CV.** Table 2 prints the baseline log10 parasite
  score BSV as "350 (185-316)": the point estimate lies above its own SIR 95%
  CI. The point estimate is encoded as printed (`omega^2 = log(1 + 3.5^2)`).
  With an exponential model on a log10-scale baseline, this produces implausibly
  wide individual baselines (see above), so treat stochastic parasite-score
  simulations with caution. Typical-value simulations are unaffected.
* **lambda_LAmB units.** Table 2 gives 1/(mg h) and the Results prose L/(mg h).
  Eq. 4 multiplies it by the MPS **amount** (mg), so 1/(mg h) is used.
* **Miltefosine bioavailability.** Equation S1 has a first-week malabsorption
  factor that was not supported in this cohort (Supplementary Results S1), so
  only `F = CumDose^-0.13` is applied. `CumDose` has no normalizing value. The
  vignette builds it as the running sum of the weight-normalized daily dose
  including the current day. At `CumDose = 0` the power function is infinite,
  so the column must be positive. Monotherapy subjects carry a placeholder of 1.
* **"More than 6-fold greater reduction in parasite score".** The Results
  compare the typical patient on combination therapy with monotherapy at
  3 months. The model gives a remaining log10 score of 0.13 versus 0.34, a
  2.6-fold ratio; Figure 3 shows about 0.05 versus 0.3. The miltefosine term
  is weaker here than in the paper's figure. Setting bioavailability to 1
  would close most of the gap, but it would also push day-21 miltefosine
  concentrations well above the Figure 1b observations. The equation and the
  values are kept as published.
* **LAmB infusion duration** is not stated; 2 hours (the usual AmBisome
  infusion) is assumed. Plasma AUC is insensitive to it.
* **Fat-free mass** is not derived from height and sex (not available); the
  virtual cohort scales it from body weight. Allometric miltefosine dosing for
  patients of 30 kg or less is not simulated.
* Region, lesion type, age, BMI and treatment arm were screened and not
  retained (Results); they are documented in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
